payload.blocks: Only how the read-only-first and explain-names rules are enforced; the rule text keeps shaping.
payload.headline: Should a check at the end of each agent turn catch permission-asking and unexplained ids?

parts.cause: The existing guard (fgos hook decision-question, src/state/decision-question.mjs) only fires when an agent calls the AskUserQuestion tool. Both frictions this morning were plain chat text, which that guard never sees. Claude Code and Codex already run fgOS hooks at the end of every turn (Stop rows for mailbox and questions in src/setup/agent-hooks.mjs), so a check there is possible.

options.cost: About 100-150 lines plus tests, one hook kind in agent-hooks.v1.json.
options.does: Add a Stop-hook check: if the last message asks permission for read-only work, or names an id (q-, p-, ds-, plan or lane name) with no plain phrase, the agent is sent back once to fix it before you see it.
options.gain: Catches both frictions in plain chat, the place they actually happened.
options.harm: Phrase matching in two languages can miss or misfire; one extra check per turn; Gemini/agy has no Stop hook, so it gets the rule only.
options.label: A. Rule + end-of-turn check

options.does: Write both rules into the always-loaded instruction; no check.
options.gain: No code, ships with the rule.
options.harm: Relies on every agent remembering; this morning shows they forget.
options.label: B. Rule text only

options.does: The AskUserQuestion guard and fgos questions ask also refuse unexplained ids.
options.harm: Misses plain chat, where both frictions happened.
options.label: C. Check only inside the question doors

parts.recommendation: A: it is the only option that reaches plain chat, where the problems happened, and it reuses the hook door that already runs at every turn end. Default if no answer: A is recorded as provisional and planned.

scope.allows: Recording the choice in DISCUSSION.md and handing it to a planner.
scope.forbids: Any code or hook change now.

parts.what: Two of this morning's frictions were an agent asking permission to do read-only work, and roles, ids and terms (like OPC) reaching you unexplained. The rule text will say both. The question is whether a program also catches them.
